$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what a reprobuild release contains.
release-pipeline.yml (called by release.yml) reads this file twice: once to build the job matrix, and once,
in the publish job, to compute the exact set of assets that must exist
before anything is made visible. Because both come from here, 'the matrix'
and 'what the release must carry' cannot drift apart -- which is what let
v0.1.0..v0.1.3 each ship a DIFFERENT subset of platforms.
Adding a leg: the bar is a GREEN BUILD OF THIS REPO on that platform, not
'a runner class exists for it'. Since the release is all-or-nothing, a row
that has never produced a binary blocks EVERY release, forever -- it does
not merely miss one asset. A runner that boots and reports its uname
proves the fleet, not the toolchain; get the platform green in ci.yml
first, then add it here. Prove, then gate.
`candidates` holds legs that are being proved. They are never built by a
tag and never part of the asset set. Dispatch release.yml from a branch
with `platforms: <platform>-<arch>` to run exactly the release leg a row
describes, on its own runner, publishing nothing; when that run is green,
move the row, unchanged, into `platforms`. A `platforms` filter on a tag
is refused, so a release is still all of `platforms` or nothing.
`candidates` is empty when nothing is being proved; linux-aarch64 was
the first row to go through it (promoted 2026-11-24).
Removing a leg is a deliberate, reviewed act: it narrows what the release
promises. Consumers on a dropped platform then fall back to the
setup-reprobuild source build with a loud warning, instead of downloading
an asset that does not exist. Never remove a leg just to get a red release
green -- fix the leg, or accept and record the narrower promise here.

$workaround: TEMPORARY: retargeted off the `eph-macos-arm64` ephemeral (tart) macOS
provider onto the static Apple-silicon runners on m3. The ephemeral
provider was spawning ZERO runners (a provider fault under separate
investigation), so every macOS release leg queued forever and no
release could ever complete. `aarch64-darwin` is the label unique to
the six healthy, idle static m3 runners (m3-mcl-001..006, which also
runner carries it, so this routes only to the static pool. These are
the same nix-darwin hosts CodeTracer's macOS jobs run green on.
REVERT to `eph-macos-arm64` once the tart macOS provider is fixed.
and a macOS leg routed there queued for over four hours.

$comment: Native, on Tart Ubuntu guests on m3 with Docker. `[self-hosted, linux,
arm64]` is matched only by the central GARM pool's runners (the m3
scale set is targeted by its name, `eph-linux-arm64`, alone).
Native rather than cross-compiled so the leg runs the same steps as
linux-x86_64 -- bootstrap, `.#release`, relocation, the multi-distro
Docker sweep and the dev-exec smoke -- on the architecture it ships.
No native package is built from it yet (`packages` names only
linux-x86_64), so the leg's package steps are skipped.
Promoted from `candidates` unchanged (only this comment differs) after
its proving run went green: release.yml dispatched on `agents`
5657bdad6 with `platforms: linux-aarch64`,
https://github.com/metacraft-labs/reprobuild/actions/runs/45380792531
(2026-11-24). Every step of the release leg passed -- bootstrap, build,
package, release-asset verification, the self-build check and the
checksum -- in 1h18m on a 4 CPU / 20 GiB / 50 GB guest, the pool's
current size. Before it, reprobuild had never built on aarch64-linux:
911 ci-reprobuild.yml jobs on this pool, none green. What changed was
io-mon b1c32599 (the Linux preload shim compiles for aarch64) and the
guests' RAM growing from 4 GiB to 20 GiB (the engine compile had been
OOM-killed, exit 137, at the old size).
Native packages built in the publish job from one platform's archive
(scripts/release/repro-build-packages.sh) and published like any other
asset: they are in the expected set, in SHA256SUMS, and signed with the
rest. After the release is public, metacraft-labs/metacraft-desktop-packages
adds them to the organisation's repositories (deb./rpm.metacraft-labs.com).
`asset` is a template; {version} is the reprobuild.nimble version.
The musl-static add-on `repro` (apps/repro-addon), one per Debian
architecture, built by scripts/build_addon_static.sh in release-pipeline.yml's
`build-addon-static` job, which runs beside the legs in the dev
environment of the `from` platform and cross-compiles arm64 and armhf
with the flake's pinned toolchains. An add-on host fetches one and pins
its digest from SHA256SUMS on the command line that runs it. `asset` is
a template; {version} is the reprobuild.nimble version, {arch} the
architecture.
`runner` is general Linux x64 capacity, not the `from` platform's
release lane: eph-linux-x64-release has one runner (infra
docs/CI-Runner-Fleet-Status.md), so a job there would wait for the
Linux leg to finish and its duration would add to the release's again.
When release.yml runs the pipeline on the reserved lane (repository
variable RELEASE_LANE=admitted), these same labels also reach infra's
`release-lane` runner group, which admits release-pipeline.yml@agents.

darwin-x86_64: No runner exists and none is planned. metacraft-dev-guidelines
policies/ci-workflow-standards.md marks macOS AMD64 'N/A -- no Intel-Mac
runner': the macOS fleet is Apple-silicon only (eph-macos-arm64 on m3).
flake.nix no longer lists x86_64-darwin among its systems either: the
pinned nixpkgs (26.11) dropped it, so nothing can be built there.
windows-aarch64: A runner DOES exist (eph-win-arm64, m3, qemu-windows-arm + swtpm,
maxRunners=2), so unlike darwin-x86_64 this is blocked by the toolchain,
not the fleet. windows/ensure-clingo.ps1 throws: 'conda-forge publishes
clingo for win-64 only ... A native ARM64 repro.exe cannot load an x64
clingo.dll.' clingo is dlopen'd at module init, so this is fatal, not
degraded. The staged runtime DLLs are x64-specific by name too
(libcrypto-3-x64.dll). Enable this row only after an ARM64 clingo exists;
adding it now would permanently block every release.
